Digestion and fermentation in the distal intestine
The fraction of ingested protein that is not digested and absorbed in the small intestine reaches the large intestine where amino acids
are not quantitatively absorbed but metabolized by the microbiota. The contributory role of colonic protein digestion may become
particularly important for people with reduced small intestinal function such as short bowel syndrome. Colonic digestion and
fermentation are important for energy production. Colonic fermentation may lead to the production of short-chain fatty acids
from undigested starch, non-starch polysaccharides, or proteins reaching the colon, providing approximately 5–10% of daily energy
requirements. In the ﬁrst steps of protein catabolism by the intestinal bacteria, these compounds are hydrolyzed by extracellular
